notes: Thread thr-mali-reads planted: 'Mae Mali'n darllen, ac mae Elen yn darllen. Ond Arth? Ond Cai?' Negatives arrive in Pennod 4, so the contrast is a pair of fragment questions.
'Ha!' is Cai's and Arth's sword cry; the coverage checker resolves it (h-prothesis of a), which is harmless.
Callback joke 'Gwellt yw enw'r dyn gwellt!' echoes Pennod 2's 'Cath yw enw'r gath!'.
Geese appear in pictures only (no lexeme), as the plan beat needs them only as scenery.

Audit-fix pass 2026-10-19 (docs/reviews/welsh-russian-lessons-2026-10-19.md): the narrator's question-and-fragment tour ('Ble mae X? Yn Y.') ran eight times; two plain ones are now statements (cut s020 'A Mali?' and s031 'Ble mae'r gogyddes?'; s021 'A dyma Mali, wrth ddrws y gegin.' keeps a pointing opener so the Mae run stays ≤ 5; s032 names the subject). Kept: s006–s007 and s015–s016 (the tour's first steps; cutting s015 too made a seven-sentence Mae run and packed new words together), s029–s030 (the reading-thread plant), s041–s042 (Arth sees the sword), s034/s077 'A Pero?' (each answered by a full sentence; s077 turns the chapter) and the closing s088. Meta-language: 'dim newid / dim treiglad' (dim is Pennod 6) replaced by arrows (b → b) in the rule, table caption, Treigladau row and A a1/a5 hints; the rule's no-change example is now bwyta (rhedeg starts with rh, which never mutates after yn, so it showed nothing). Pensa: b1 'Pero … ___ wrth y wal' also fitted bwyta/yfed, now cued by nos da; b6 'Mae ___ mawr yn y neuadd' also fitted cleddyf, now contrasts the small window with the hall's ___ (drws); A a3 and C c1–c4, c6 accept fronted identification, pronoun subjects and fuller answers.

[?] 'mae Cai'n goch' for 'Cai is red in the face': natural without 'wyneb'?
[?] Verbless exclamatory list in narration: acceptable style?
[?] 'Ond Arth? Ond Cai?' as the implied negative contrast: clear enough?

grammar.nodyn_en: Mae … yn + a verb-noun means '… is doing' or '… does': Mae Arth yn rhedeg 'Arth is running'. Unlike yn before an adjective (yn goch, yn gyflym), yn before a verb-noun never mutates it: yn gweld, yn bwyta, yn darllen. Two actions can share one mae: mae e'n rhedeg ac yn bwyta.
